['show','--first-parent','-m','--name-only'] : ['show','--name-only']`. **`tk-2026-08-19` (s2076) replaced that with a single unconditional `git show --pretty=format: --name-only` for every commit**, under a header comment reading *"Same shape as artifacts/tk-2026-08-18/classify.mjs"* — an assertion of sameness about a file the author had just rewritten. ⚠️ **WHY THAT IS WRONG AND NOT MERELY DIFFERENT: for a true merge commit `git show --name-only` prints the COMBINED diff, which is empty for any path that matches one parent.** A merge that lands player code therefore reports **zero files** and is filed as *bookkeeping* — the exact bucket a digest uses to say *"no player-visible change landed."* 🕳️ **THE REASON NOBODY SAW IT, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE HALF: `2026-08-19` had 47 commits and `0` merges.** A defect in merge handling cannot manifest on a day with no merges, so the regression's own landing day was the one day in the retained window that could not test it — and the digest it produced (*"zero merges … the county stood still for a day"*) was **correct**, which is worse than a visible red, because a correct output is read as evidence the instrument works. 📊 **PRICED ON FIRST EXPOSURE. `2026-08-20`: 180 first-parent commits, `30` merge commits.** Inherited unchanged the classifier reports **21** player-visible; the correct method reports **28**. **7 merges invisible**, and **4 of them are headlines in the digest I just filed** — `20895457a` **e7-dead-band, an entire new map (+10 player files, read as 0)** · `db3d10076` worn-out machines / alive cap (+6, owner-ruled) · `8086ee597` the season roll (+2) · `9dca85081` the deepwater claim re-admission (+6). The other 3 (`9d902829a`, `fd6b6952c`, `5ca1c00c9`) were dismissals either way, so the damage would have been silent in both directions. ✅ **NO PUBLISHED DIGEST IS FALSE — VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, AND I CHECKED BEFORE I ACCUSED.** My first back-check flagged `2026-08-15` as under-reported (legacy 1 → fixed 6) and I did **not** file that: I read `artifacts/tk-2026-08-15/classify.mjs` first and found it carries the merge-safe branch, so its digest's `6 touching src/public/assets` and its five merge headlines were right when written. **The gap was in my control, not in that digest.** Across the whole retained window only `08-15` and `08-20` contain merges touching player paths; `08-18`'s 3 merges genuinely touch none (`fixed = 0`, matching its published `0`); `08-16`/`08-17`/`08-19` have zero merges. **The regression existed for exactly one digest and that digest was unaffected.** 🔧 **THE CURE, AND ITS HONEST LIMIT.** `artifacts/tk-2026-08-20/classify.mjs` lists files as `git diff --name-only <sha>^1 <sha>` — the right question for a `--first-parent` walk (*what did this commit bring onto main relative to its first parent*), correct for merges and identical to `--name-only` for ordinary commits. **CONTROLLED, not asserted: across all 180 of yesterday's commits it agrees with the `08-15`-lineage `show --first-parent -m` method on `180/180`**, so it RESTORES the lineage rather than inventing a third method. It also **computes both methods every run and prints every disagreement**, so the next fire that copies it forward carries the control with it and a future silent revert announces itself in the output. ⚠️ **That defence lives in the artifact that gets copied forward, so it survives exactly as long as the copying does — it is not a guard and I am not claiming it is one.** 🚫 **NO GUARD IS PROPOSED, DELIBERATELY.** These classifiers are per-day retained evidence, not a run surface; a battery test over `artifacts/tk-*/` would red on every historical file the RETENTION LAW forbids editing, and would be excused into uselessness within a week (the `cross-engine` label's fate, F-1460-1). 💡 **THE GENERAL SHAPE, worth more than the instance: a regression that lands on a day containing no instances of the thing it breaks is invisible BY CONSTRUCTION, and its clean output is actively misleading. When a copied-forward instrument is rewritten, the comment claiming continuity is the author's INTENT, never a measurement — diff it against its stated ancestor, and price it against the busiest day it will meet rather than the day it lands on.** ⓘ Also caught by my own pre-commit verifier: a hand-typed hash `c61ed4dc` for `b3ed55bb1` (dropped a `d`), which resolves to nothing — the F-1633-1 wrong-needle class, found because the digest's hashes were checked against `git` rather than re-read.
